title: Auto Loans: Loan Balance and Interest Build-up for a Scheduled Payment
content:
For a scheduled Auto Loans payment that PCB makes out of a borrower's checking account on an installment in arrears, the balance lent and the interest it has built up are both reconstructed from the loan's activity in the manner set out here.

## Balance lent

The balance of money lent that is still unrepaid is rebuilt from the activity: the disbursement made at funding, less the part of every payment received that went to reduce that balance, plus every payment reversal. It is stated to the cent.

## Interest built up

The interest is that balance times the APR over one hundred, spread across the product's day count, times the calendar days from the last payment date, leaving that day out, through the credit date, counting that day in. For this payment the credit date is the day on which it is booked. The interest is rounded half-up to the cent a single time, on the final interest figure; nothing is rounded along the way.

## Day count illustration (hypothetical dates)

A last payment date of 15 March and a credit date of 2 April give 18 days: the sixteen days from 16 March to 31 March, and 1 and 2 April.

## Rounding illustration (invented figures)

If one day's unrounded interest came to 1.80274 and 23 days had run, the interest is 41.46302 before rounding and 41.46 after the single rounding.

## Balance illustration (invented activity)

Disbursement 24000.00; the parts of all payments so far that reduced the balance lent total 3150.00; one payment reversal of 315.00. The balance lent is 24000.00 less 3150.00 plus 315.00, which comes to 21165.00.
